name: Doublo HIFU
lead: Doublo is an intense focused ultrasound (IFUS, also called HIFU) device made by HIRONIC Co. of Seongnam, Korea, used for noninvasive skin tightening of the face and neck [1][2]. The goal is a firmer, lifted look along the jawline and lower face without surgery: ultrasound energy is focused to heat tissue beneath the skin surface, which is meant to prompt collagen remodelling and tightening [1][3].

A 2015 study by Suh and colleagues in the Journal of Cosmetic and Laser Therapy treated 11 patients with facial laxity (mean age 46) and took skin biopsies before treatment and two months afterwards. Blinded investigators rated photographic improvement, and the authors reported more collagen fibres in the lower dermis and between fat layers [1]. A 2020 prospective study of 43 patients with neck and lower-face laxity by Friedman and colleagues reported the authors' experience with the Doublo device [2].
Researchers describe IFUS as a nonablative technology with a good safety profile, noting that most clinical studies have examined a different system, the Ulthera device [2].

chain: Focused ultrasound heats tissue at set depths beneath the skin
The thermal effect prompts new collagen in the dermis and deeper layers
Skin of the lower face and neck looks tighter over the following weeks
angle.text: Doublo treatments are used to tighten mild sagging along the jawline and neck without surgery. The 2015 study found more collagen on biopsy two months after treatment, and the 2020 study reported benefit for selected patients with minor sagging [1][2].

paras: Intense focused ultrasound produces thermal effects at various depths while sparing the overlying tissue, and is used for skin laxity [1]. The 2020 paper characterises it as a nonablative skin-tightening technology [2]. General background on focused ultrasound notes that the focal point is heated to roughly 65 to 85 degrees Celsius and that tissue held above 60 degrees for more than a second is irreversibly damaged, which is the basis of the thermal effect [3].

In the 2015 study, two handpieces with focal depths of 3 mm and 4.5 mm were used for three to five passes, spaced 1 to 2 mm apart [1]. Results are assessed weeks to months later, since the proposed mechanism is new collagen formation after thermal injury [1].

At two months in the 2015 study, subjective improvement was 63.6% and objective improvement was 72.7%. Staining of biopsies showed increased collagen fibres in the lower dermis and between fat layers, and the authors called the technique effective and safe in this small group of Asian patients [1].

The 2020 study, in which two independent dermatologists scored response on a 0 to 5 scale, concluded that ultrasound appears to be a safe modality for skin tightening in selected patients with minor sagging and no volume discrepancy. Its abstract reports erythema and edema that were acute and transient [2].

Two published studies examine Doublo. The 2015 study had 11 patients with biopsies and blinded photographic assessment [1]. The 2020 prospective study included 43 patients with neck and lower-face laxity [2]. A registered trial (NCT04157218, status unknown) planned to compare thread lifting and microfocused ultrasound for face tightening in 45 participants [4].

card.note: Evidence is limited to two small studies.

quick.overview:
Doublo is a Korean-made focused-ultrasound device used to tighten facial and neck skin.

Two small studies (11 and 43 patients) have been published; one authors' group described the technology as safe but of limited efficacy.
quick.mechanism: Focused ultrasound creates heat at various depths below the skin surface while sparing the surface layer.
quick.risks: The 2020 study describes IFUS as having a good safety profile; details beyond that were not available in the reviewed sources.
